quest.title: Proof of Strength
quest.description: What can serve as a symbol of one's power...?
quest.rewards_formatted: Hero's Wit x3, Guide to Resistance x3, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Slazhnev
dialogues.text: ...If you wanna know who's the strongest warrior, haha, look no further than our captain! He can hold back the Abyss with pure physical power alone!

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Ha! Exactly the sort of drivel I'd expect from someone who's never seen real combat! D'you think powerful warriors just stand around hitting wooden dummies? Besides, even if we're talking raw strength, I doubt he's a match for our Grand Master...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Ugh, that's enough! I didn't invite you both here to listen to you bicker.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Lohen? And isn't that...Leifhelm and Slazhnev? What are you guys doing together, and what brings you two all this way from Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hah... I heard there were a couple of "combatologists" in Nod-Krai, so I invited them over to help me compile a "Formidable Foes Fieldbook".

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: If only I'd known combatologists were so darn combative... *sigh* Guess I'm gonna have to knock their heads together and see if I can't get them to be a bit more professional.

dialogues.speaker: Slazhnev
dialogues.text: Ahaha... I—I'll start drawing up a list right away! Ehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: C—Captain Lohen! I'm not trying to be uncooperative, it's just that the word "formidable" is far too vague.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Never mind regular monsters — even the power gap between the Archons is huge. If we don't find a suitable benchmark, I'm afraid any further discussion will be pointless...

dialogues.speaker: Slazhnev
dialogues.text: If we're talking about a benchmark of power that everyone can accept... we should probably go with dragons, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Dragons?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously? Paimon feels like the power gaps between dragons aren't much smaller than those between the Archons...

choices.text: Why do you want to compile a Formidable Foes Fieldbook, anyway?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Well... Long story short, after a period of reflection, I concluded that the best way to get even stronger was to challenge the most powerful opponents from all over the world.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...Isn't that what you were already doing before?)

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: But then earlier this morning, just as I was about to set off... this weird-looking thing appeared in front of me and started talking a bunch of nonsense.

response.speaker: Strange-Looking Object
response.text: "Lost human, thrice shall you face the might of the dragon. Then, and only then, will you comprehend the true meaning of strength."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That sounds like something Barbeloth would say...)

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I'm not one for believing in prophecies, but... Hmph, well let's just say that I feel like I'm being played here, and I don't like it one bit.

response.speaker: Leifhelm
response.text: Dragons, huh... Here in Mondstadt, you'd have to be talking about Dvalin or Ursa the Drake, or else those legends about Dragonspine... Hmm, what else is there?

response.speaker: Slazhnev
response.text: Hah, well clearly that's where your knowledge falls short! According to top-secret intel I acquired in Nod-Krai, a powerful ancient dragon has recently snuck into Dornman Port!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously!? No way...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: If we want the truth, there's only one way to find out.

choices.text: Sure sounds like "dragons" got your attention…

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ineffa! Ineffa! Did you see that windmill!? I need you to make a record of how it works!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Understood — preparing to photograph the windmill. Would you like to be included in the picture this time?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: #Huh? {NICKNAME} and Paimon? And Lohen!? Hey there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhhh... Intel from Nod-Krai about a powerful ancient dragon... Paimon sees what's going on!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Assessing situation... It appears that Mr. Lohen hopes to fight me. Is that correct?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: In a nutshell, yes — that's exactly what I was hoping to do. Back when the expedition was in Nod-Krai, I had no reason to suspect you had such an extraordinary history.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: But that's all by the by. I've been wanting to test my skills against you for quite some time now, so... How about it?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hehe! Ineffa, show him who's boss!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: My apologies — according to today's schedule, we still have to visit Mondstadt to collect some special components. My assessments indicate that fighting you now may impact our subsequent operations.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... I almost forgot! We heard there was some sort of giant robot in Mondstadt... That's why we're here! But then I got a little side-tracked...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: It's alright... I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lohen... You're not seriously giving up just like that!?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: If I help you deal with the Ruin Guards, that should clear up your schedule, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hmm... This one here?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ineffa! Strip it for parts!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Such fluid movements... I'd never have guessed you were a machine.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Your attacks are also very precise, Mr. Lohen. Almost mechanically so.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Woohoo, new parts, hehe! I'm gonna be able to create some excellent new modules with these!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: And... Uhm... Does this mean you're free to...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ineffa, look for more! I want as many as we can get!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Understood... My apologies, Mr. Lohen. We can talk about this later.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After much exploration...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Zzz... Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aino's asleep... Did she wear herself out playing in Dornman Port?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: She's often like this — her batteries drain quickly. I am sorry, Mr. Lohen, but I'm afraid I can't get up right now. I must stay here until Aino has entered a deeper state of sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...That's quite all right. I've already seen enough to know what you're capable of.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...I hope my combat data provides some useful insights.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: By the way, the person who told us about these special mechanisms also mentioned Dragonspine. You might want to go there and check things out...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Seeker of Power, Follower of Fate, you are here at last.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's Durin... Paimon's really not surprised at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's something odd about the way he's speaking...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: A sovereign ruler, the creation of a mage, and a descendant of angels... All wield disparate powers, yet all were crowned as dragons.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...This is because dragons are the symbol of power.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: So "doing battle with great dragons" became a way to prove your strength? Huh. I think I might be starting to understand the founding Grand Master a little better.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I can see you still have much to say, but I suggest we cross blades instead. After all, a single sword stroke is worth a thousand words!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: W—Wait! Y—Young human, the trial you seek is far from here. You must venture to Stormterror's Lair and face the final prophecy!

choices.text: Why is he talking so fast?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you alright, Durin? You sound kinda weird today.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: (Ahhh, phew... I think I got through the important bits... even if I did have to skip a lot!)

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Uhm, I think Albedo said he needed help with an experiment, so I'd better be heading back now. Sorry, everyone!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Well he sure left in a hurry... What a shame.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hey, what's this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhm... Why exactly was Durin here? Apart from that last line about "venturing to Stormterror's Lair," he just seemed to be talking nonsense...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Interesting. I'm getting curious as to exactly how this "prophecy" will come true...

choices.text: ...He was only here so that the next dragon counts as number three.
He sounds like an actor who wants to get off stage!

talks.objective: Seek the Dragon of the East

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Wonderful... Now, according to Barbeloth's prophecy, the human in need of guidance should be here in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Entrance lines... memorized. Entrance effects... confirmed. Hehe, nothing can go wrong this time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... Why do you guys think the "final prophecy" needs Lohen to come here?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh no, they're here already? Did Durin not finish his lines? Ugh... I need to keep quiet...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could the final "might of the dragon" be talking about Dvalin? He doesn't seem to be here today, though...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Technically speaking, I already saw him when I first returned home from Nod-Krai. He was right beside you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! In Wolvendom, when you were delivering letters for Varka! Wait... So does that mean the prophecy has been fulfilled already?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: If we're being generous with our interpretation, then technically, I've already "thrice faced the might of the dragon."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But do you "comprehend the true meaning of strength" yet?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I guess that's why the prophecy has guided me here...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Before this place was known as Stormterror's Lair, it was the God of Storms, Decarabian's domain.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: But the mighty god who could conjure storms to shut out the world couldn't stem the yearning for freedom within his own walls of wind.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Yet the God of the North Wind, with whom he had once vied for the divine throne, found the answer he had always sought only after abandoning his power.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Huh? There seems to be more to this kid than Varka led me to believe...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: The Mirror of the Dawning Morn, Durin... For a time, they too were lost to confusion and doubt. What led them to strength was more than just power.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well, well... You really seem to be getting it!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: And Ursa too, the monster who had once been an angel.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks you might be on to something here, Lohen... But, uhm, you're speaking kinda funny...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: "The angel who chose power still yearned to remain close to humanity, eventually falling to become a pitiful monster..."

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: "O humans who have witnessed this all, do you still aspire to power?"

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Hey! Those are my lines!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wha—!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Oh dear... The cat's out of the bag now, isn't it?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: A pleasure to meet you, Lady Nicole. I've read your script, and I have to say, I was very impressed.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: *sigh*... Why do I get the feeling that Durin dropped his copy?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Oh? So that was part of the prophecy, too?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Not at all. If I'd known in advance, I wouldn't have just... *cough*.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Regardless, it was a well-written script. Very entertaining — as a heartwarming little fairy tale, of course. I must say though, I'm not a huge fan of being lectured to... not even by an angel.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...I'll choose to believe that was aimed at my former colleague — the one who chose power.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Seeing as you've read my script, I suppose you already know everything I have to say?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Indeed, and I'll make sure to treat it as valued advice. Now, was there anything else — or can I get back to compiling my Formidable Foes Fieldbook?

choices.text: (He didn't say he plans to follow that advice...)

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: I must admit though, it's been quite a productive day. I'm sure I must've gotten a tiny bit stronger, at least...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Thank you, everyone... and give my regards to the production crew!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: *sigh*... Why are humans always so difficult to deal with?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhm, can someone tell Paimon what's going on? She's feeling... very, very confused...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Do you remember dealing with Dottore and the poison left behind by Ursa in Mondstadt? I'm told that Lohen also endured his fair share of suffering around that time.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Since that was a calamity caused by a former angel, it naturally fell on a current angel to set things right... Though "things" didn't go exactly how I planned...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: It seems that humanity's fate is destined to become ever more unpredictable... The guidance of angels is no longer the only thing leading them toward the future.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But all those infinite possibilities... Perhaps that is precisely where humanity's true strength lies?

choices.text: (Pretty sure he's just gonna keep compiling his fieldbook, whatever she says...)
Why does everyone sound like they're reading from a script?

dialogues.speaker: Slazhnev
dialogues.text: Our captain isn't just strong — he even developed a compound that counters the Abyss! Bet you didn't know that, did you, smartypants? And yet you think I'm a "false expert" who doesn't know anything!?

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Well, do you know about our Grand Master's amazing speed? He used the Ley Lines to travel all the way from Nod-Krai to Mondstadt in less time than it takes you to tie your shoelaces — if you even know how!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: *sigh* Still, even if it was my first attempt, I can't believe this is how things turned out...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, it didn't really end badly!

choices.text: Your first attempt at what, though?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Hah... My first Witch's Homework. I'll explain it all later.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Hmm... This one here?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ineffa! Strip it for parts!
